correctness.rationale: A real circular BV derivative is a finite zero-mass signed measure; any antipodal atom difference has a semicircle step as its primitive. The Jordan product representation with the factor V/2 makes the BV quotient bounded by the maximum probability TV distance of two kernel translates, and two atoms attain it. The Jacobi product gives k_t'(u)<0 for 0<u<π, so for separation h the positive region of the density difference is the semicircle (h/2−π,h/2), with TV derivative k_t(h/2)−k_t(π−h/2)>0 for 0<h<π. At h=π this gives the semicircle mass formula and integrating the Fourier heat density gives the alternating odd series. Equality requires that almost every pair sampled independently from the two normalized Jordan parts is antipodal; hence both parts must be opposite singleton atoms. Strict time decrease follows by differentiating the semicircle integral to get 4k_t'(π/2); strict submultiplicativity follows because an attaining semicircle step becomes nonconstant and smooth after any positive time and so cannot attain the second quotient. Positivity and K<1 follow from strict radial decrease and strict kernel positivity. For a=π/2 the wrapped Gaussian differs from the unwrapped two-sided outside tail only on |u|≥3a, so 1−K(t)=4Φ(−a/√(2t))+O(exp(−9a²/(4t))). The first two Mills terms give the stated constants; the first two odd Fourier modes and the exponentially smaller tail give the large-time expansion. Replay: RESULT.md lines 33–71. VERIFICATION.md and verification/check_heat_bv.py were inspected, not run; their finite samples are not a universal certificate.
